clinician.trajectory_summary: A 52-year-old male presented with right lower quadrant abdominal pain and tenderness. He underwent surgery and subsequently developed hypoxia with tachypnea requiring supplemental oxygen and exertional dyspnea on postoperative day 1. There were no clinical signs of deep venous thrombosis such as calf or thigh swelling, erythema, edema, tenderness, or palpable cords. The patient had no prior history of venous thromboembolism or known hypercoagulable states. A CT pulmonary angiography was ordered to evaluate for pulmonary embolism. Despite no documented venous Doppler ultrasound or other confirmatory imaging reports available in the source, the final diagnosis was a massive saddle pulmonary embolism.
